title: Analyzing Key Predictors of Heart Attack Risk: A Machine Learning Approach
content: Heart disease remains a leading cause of mortality worldwide, with early identification of at-risk individuals being critical for prevention. This study applies machine learning techniques to a comprehensive dataset to identify key predictors of heart attack risk. Logistic regression analysis identified BMI, age, hypertension, family history, and cholesterol levels as significant predictors of heart attack risk. Notably, individuals with BMI > 30 were 2.5 times more likely to be in the high-risk category, and the risk increased by 8% with each additional year of age. The model achieved strong predictive performance and highlighted that regular physical activity reduced heart attack risk by up to 20%. These findings offer valuable insights for targeted prevention strategies and public health policy, underscoring the potential of machine learning in cardiovascular risk assessment.
